learningObjective: Distinguish a frequentist confidence procedure's long-run coverage from a Bayesian credible interval's posterior probability statement.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG places repeated confidence intervals and one posterior distribution on aligned parameter axes, making the different sources of randomness spatially explicit. Mermaid was rejected because this is interval geometry rather than a flow; semantic HTML would make exact endpoints and coverage harder to compare; interaction would add state without improving the fixed distinction; paper-figure reuse was unnecessary and reuse permission was not established; mixed media would add complexity; and no visual would leave the article's most commonly confused interpretation in prose.

pages.insight: The deck frames Bayesian inference as integration over probability mass and lists computational methods for posterior expectations.
The deck introduces sampling variance by showing that point estimates change across realizations of the data-generating population.
The deck contrasts maximum likelihood and MAP point estimates with Bayesian estimation of a parameter distribution.
The Bayes-rule overview separates prior belief, likelihood, posterior belief, and evidence before parameter learning.
The summary slide contrasts MLE, Bayesian estimation, and MAP by whether learning returns one parameter value or a distribution.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages were text-searched, and relevant slides 7, 16-17, and 80-81 were inspected with neighboring pages 6, 8, 18, and 82. No slide explains confidence-versus-credible interval semantics. The original figure therefore extends the deck's sampling-variance and parameter-distribution distinction rather than reproducing a deck layout.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods: Confidence Intervals
sources.usage: Used to verify that a confidence interval is generated by a sampling procedure and that its width reflects sampling uncertainty.
sources.license: No NIST text, data, or figure copied; statistical definitions were consulted and the visual geometry is original.

sources.title: An Introduction to Bayesian Reasoning and Methods: Comparing Bayesian and frequentist interval estimates
sources.usage: Used to verify the repeated-sampling interpretation of confidence level and the posterior-probability interpretation of a credible interval.
sources.license: The book is published under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, but no prose or figure is reused; only the underlying statistical definitions inform an original redraw.

sources.title: Stan Reference Manual: Effective sample size
sources.usage: Used to verify that posterior quantities such as quantiles are estimated from correlated MCMC draws and require effective-sample-size diagnostics.
sources.license: Stan documentation is BSD-3-Clause, but no documentation text, code, or figure is copied; implementation semantics are referenced only.

sourceReview.notes: No source figure was needed. Because reuse permission for any candidate interval graphic was not established, the implementation is an original, illustrative construction with no empirical data and no copied layout.

agentReview.summary: Selected the interval interpretation as the hardest mental model. Recommended a compact static SVG that encodes frequentist coverage through repeated rows and Bayesian credibility through posterior area, with labels and line styles carrying all meaning without color.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a title and detailed description; panel headings, row labels, solid versus dashed interval lines, endpoint brackets, a fixed-parameter reference line, and explicit equations communicate the distinction without color. Its 360-pixel viewBox scales to a 390 CSS-pixel viewport, uses shared theme variables for dark mode, and inherits the shared print palette.
